critique: The complete-class and strict-separation results are confined to finite binary schedules, and the resulting general program has exponentially many schedule constraints. The strict advantage over the published quadratic class is proved for one engineered six-coordinate experiment and its independent products, not for a broad natural design family or the cited school-network design. The inference theorem covers independent blocks under a separate denominator-LLN condition and does not transfer the construction to connected interference designs. The framing accurately leaves the school-network computation open and does not claim finite-sample coverage, scalable computation, or real-outcome applicability.
